idiom_name: MQTTNIO (SwiftNIO) client with a broker-held persistent session
implementation_notes: Swift has no JVM-style durable-subscription API, so the realization is MQTTNIO - the swift-server-community MQTT 3.1.1/5.0 client - paired with a broker that keeps the session. Structurally, the broker's session replaces the classic subscription registry and backlog: subscribe with QoS atLeastOnce, reuse the same client identifier on every reconnect, and set the session expiry (MQTT 5) or disable the clean session (3.1.1) so publications are queued while the client is offline. Application code owns the rest - acknowledgement, deduplication and catch-up bounding - because the client library deliberately does not persist in-flight state.
pitfalls: MQTTNIO opens a fresh connection per withConnection block and unsubscribes when the closure exits, so the session (and its queued backlog) only survives if the broker-side session settings and the client identifier are configured deliberately.
The client does not persist in-flight QoS state, so at-least-once redelivery is the expected behaviour after a restart and the handler must deduplicate.
Subscription closures are async sequences on SwiftNIO event loops: doing blocking work inside the loop starves the connection and can trip the keep-alive timeout.
